bug_semantics: The unauthenticated static-download route passes request.getParameter("version") into BaseUtils.replaceFileNameAndExtension without validating it. For a request to the route base (/file/static/noauth in the renamed endpoint, formerly /downloadFile/static/noauth), the path-derived fileName is "noauth", whose full-path component is empty, so the helper replaces it entirely with attacker-controlled version. A value such as ../../etc/passwd is then handed to FileUtils.readFile(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName, ...), which constructs new File(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName) and can escape the intended download directory, exposing arbitrary readable files without authentication.
flaw_origin: Commit b34987f7b37b5fd6a03b9dd9092bd18efc936d46 added version as a cache/content-identity filename override during a resources/web-client refactor. The normal producer generated an ID for version, but DownloadFileRequestHandler treated the HTTP parameter as if it were trusted and reused it as a filesystem child path. The already-existing security rule exempted /downloadFile/static/noauth/** from authentication, making this new trust-boundary error remotely reachable immediately.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file commit b34987f7b37b5fd6a03b9dd9092bd18efc936d46` shows human author AlexKirkouski <alex.kirkouski@gmail.com> and the same human committer, subject `Resources / web client refactoring`, and no body or trailers; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other commit-object AI marker.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/lsfusion/platform/issues/1543 identifies unauthenticated `/file/static/noauth` plus attacker-controlled `version`, the handler path, arbitrary file read, and affected versions through 6.1. In the validated full-history clone, `git log -L 44,46:web-client/src/main/java/lsfusion/http/controller/file/DownloadFileRequestHandler.java 9dc9a7889f8120d6bd6802c09b374639642cbcb9^` resolves the complete vulnerable three-line version block to b34987f7b37b5fd6a03b9dd9092bd18efc936d46; reverse `git log -S'request.getParameter("version")'` over both historical handler paths finds the same sole introduction. `git show b34987...` shows the exact addition: read `version`, test only for non-null, then call `BaseUtils.replaceFileNameAndExtension(fileName, version)`. At that tree, BaseUtils.java implements that helper as `FilenameUtils.getFullPath(filePath) + toName`; FileUtils.java:57 reads `createFile(relativePath, fileName)`, and createFile at line 81 is `new File(relativePath, fileName)`. The same BIC tree's applicationContext-security.xml:39-44 exempts `/downloadFile/static/noauth/**` and requires authentication only for the remaining `/downloadFile/**`. Direct parent-tree verification is concrete: `git show 51dd90c21ec7e7b289fde206208106cf80b835f8:web-client/src/main/java/lsfusion/http/controller/file/DownloadFileRequestHandler.java` contains the path extraction and FileUtils.readFile sink but no `version` parameter read or filename replacement, while `git diff 51dd90c... b34987f... -- <handler>` adds exactly those four vulnerable lines. Tag ancestry establishes the boundary: `git tag --contains b34987...` returns 5.0-beta0, 5.0, 5.1, all 6.0 tags, 6.1, and 6.2, while 4.1 does not contain it; thus repository history narrows the advisory's unbounded `<= 6.1` statement to introduction beginning with 5.0-beta0. Original fix 9dc9a7889f8120d6bd6802c09b374639642cbcb9 (`Fixed unauthorized arbitrary file read (closes #1543)`) rejects version values containing `..` with HTTP 400 before replacement. Release-bearing commit d828168524d47f78426b68a58ef7905eb2d4dca0 applies the identical patch and records `(cherry picked from commit 9dc9a788...)`; `git tag --contains d828168...` returns 6.2, while no tag contains 9dc9a788... and 6.1 contains neither fix. Therefore 6.1 remains vulnerable and 6.2 contains the fix, despite the advisory snapshot's null first_patched_version.
reasoning: The vulnerable mechanism is not merely the later endpoint rename: commit 256ae9dcb19d8762b1cb43f2d1e688d46592581c changed `/downloadFile` to `/file` while preserving both the unauthenticated `static/noauth` exception and the pre-existing unvalidated version override. Following the vulnerable lines through blame, `git log -L`, and string-pickaxe history reaches b34987f7b37b5fd6a03b9dd9092bd18efc936d46, which first introduced the trust-boundary crossing into an already public route and filesystem sink. Its immediate parent proves absence, so the later rename, refactors, release commits, and fix cherry-pick are not BICs. The BIC is a single-parent repository commit whose vulnerable hunk is directly present; no smaller member commit is exposed in the clone, so no squash decomposition is claimed. The original direct fix is 9dc9a7889f8120d6bd6802c09b374639642cbcb9; d828168524d47f78426b68a58ef7905eb2d4dca0 is its explicit cherry-pick and the fix object actually contained by release tag 6.2. Finally, attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object: it has only human AlexKirkouski author/committer metadata and no AI trailer or bot marker. That supports the closed NOT_AI verdict independently of any later history.
